description: I'm a Mechatronics and Autonomous Systems Engineering student at Liverpool John Moores University.
summary: "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" explores NASA’s footprint on the Moon and Mars. This project looks at the retired hardware on Mars and the Moon, including Apollo descent stages, laser retroreflectors, and Mars rovers (Spirit, Opportunity, InSight, and Ingenuity). This project allows us to see how the retired hardware can be used as scientific labs and orbital reference points, and how it serves as an important part of history for future planetary exploration.
details:
Over decades of space exploration, we have left a lasting legacy on other planets in the solar system, and this project aims to demonstrate how retired hardware from NASA’s exploration of the moon and Mars can be viewed as a narrative by identifying how it aids science, tracking, and planning.

This provides great insight into how historical missions inform future planning. It can be used for educational purposes and to provide engineers with a benchmark for future Artemis crews.

Data Sources
NASA Open Data: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC), LOLA elevation data, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (HiRISE), and NASA PDS Geosciences Node.

Creativity
This project features a creative concept by examining how abandoned hardware can be viewed as an active lab. The narrative was carefully crafted to be both accurate and engaging, balancing natural human language with precise NASA data.
